sentences.text: This dinosaur possessed large hands that closely resembled those found in the Heterodontosauridae family.
Its limbs were significantly long, a trait similar to that of later heterodontosaurids.
The tibia measured as long as the femur, indicating it was a fast runner.
It possessed unusually large hands capable of grasping objects.
The morphology of its triangular teeth suggests it was partially herbivorous.
The holotype specimen, catalogued as SAM-PK-K8025, was collected in 1993 from the Upper Elliot Formation in Free State, South Africa.
The type species Eocursor parvus was formally described in 2007 by Richard J. Butler, Roger M. H. Smith, and David B. Norman.
Eocursor lived at the beginning of the Jurassic period, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago, between the Hettangian and Sinemurian stages, in what is now Africa.

The exact age of Eocursor is debated; it was originally interpreted as Late Triassic (around 210 million years ago), but later studies suggest it is Early Jurassic, though independent geochronological support for its assumed age remains lacking.
